name: Nap (Napoleon)
description: Nap (short for Napoleon) is a classic English trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in Britain during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is a quick, high-stakes game where players bid on how many of their five cards they can win in a trick-based battle against everyone else. It is known for its escalating bidding tiers named after Napoleonic battles (Wellington, BlÃ¼cher) and its simple yet ruthless scoring system.

history.origins: Napoleon is a classic English pub game first documented in H.E. Heather's October 1875 edition of The Bazaar. It quickly became England's national five-card game, displacing Loo. The expression 'going Nap' (meaning to risk all on one attempt) derives from this game.
timeline: 1875: Earliest rules published by H.E. Heather in The Bazaar
1885: American Hoyle incorrectly claims French origin; more likely European roots
1891: Bids of Wellington, BlÃ¼cher and MisÃ¨re added
1982: Andrew Pennycook notes Nap was 'widely played in pubs'
Present: Still played in parts of Britain
history.cultural: A quintessential British pub game played for small stakes. The terminology reflects British military history, with bids named after the Duke of Wellington and General BlÃ¼cher who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo.
history.evolution: The game evolved from simple five-card bidding to include advanced bids like Wellington and BlÃ¼cher. Variants emerged including Peep Nap, Purchase Nap, and multi-card versions.

setup.players: 3-8 players; 4-5 is optimal. No permanent partnerships.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. Often reduced based on player count.
setup.dealing: Five cards to each playerâ€”either 3 then 2, or 2 then 3. Cards shuffled only at start and after successful Nap/Wellington/BlÃ¼cher.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips or counters for stakes.

rules.objective: Win at least the number of tricks bid. The bidder plays against all other players who form a temporary team.
rules.gameplay: 1. Bidding: Each player has one chance to bid, starting left of dealer. Must pass or bid higher than previous. Bids in ascending order: Three (3 tricks), Four (4 tricks), Nap (5 tricks), Wellington (5 tricks, higher stakesâ€”can only bid after Nap), BlÃ¼cher (5 tricks, highest stakesâ€”can only bid after Wellington). 2. High bidder leads first trick; suit of this card becomes trumps. 3. Players must follow suit if possible. 4. Highest trump wins trick; if no trumps, highest card of led suit wins. 5. Winner of trick leads next.
keyRules: Five cards each; high bidder names trumps by leading
One bidding round onlyâ€”pass or overcall
Wellington can only be bid after Nap; BlÃ¼cher only after Wellington
Cards often not shuffled between hands (just cut)

strategy.basic: Be aggressive with your bids if you have a high trump (Ace or King) and at least one other card of the same suit. Since you only have 5 cards, a single strong suit can carry the whole hand. If you aren't the bidder, your only goal is to 'break' the bid by taking just one trick.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Overbid' Defense: If you have a solid hand (e.g., King and Queen of a suit) and someone bids 3, you should consider bidding 4 just to prevent them from taking the pot. Even if you fail, you prevent them from certain victory and force them to play defensively next round.
strategy.advanced: Counting the BlÃ¼cher: Only bid Wellington or BlÃ¼cher if you hold the Ace and King of your lead suit. If someone else holds the Ace, they will almost certainly 'break' you on the first trick. Wellington is a psychological tool to scare away weaker 'Nap' bidders.
tips: If you are a defender, always lead through the bidder to try and find their weak suit
In Nap, the Ace is your most important cardâ€”never waste it on a trick where someone else has already played a trump unless you have to
With a balanced hand and no strong suit, consider passing rather than bidding low

variations.name: Peep Nap
variations.description: Extra card dealt face-down to table. Players may pay to privately view it before bidding.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Peep Nap adds a floater card and peep payment; overrides not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Stake-based payment system. Bidder wins stakes from all opponents if successful; pays all opponents if unsuccessful.
scoring.winCondition: Win at least the number of tricks bid.

synthesis.shortDescription: A spirited British trick-taking game where players bid on winning tricks with just five cards. Famous for its Napoleonic bidding tiers.
